metadata.author: V2 expansion (subagent draft)
metadata.key_test: Refined Strategy 3 (complexity control) -- but achieved through INSTITUTIONAL quality in a low-complexity environment, NOT through Singapore-style demographic engineering or constrained voice. Mauritius is genuinely multi-ethnic and genuinely democratic; high P1 (0.614) + democratic accountability should predict durable stability. The test is whether the framework attributes the success to institutions rather than to island geography alone.
metadata.notes: Reference-based record (country_ref + years; no embedded indicators). Resolved scores are real MI v2 re-scores. Replaces the original Case 49 (Singapore standalone) per the revisions/replacements doc, to gain an independent, never-before-scored entity. 1968 independence -> 2024; scored ~1996 vs 2024. Notably, P1 actually ROSE (0.614 -> 0.637) -- a rare improving-institutions case in this batch -- and MI was near-flat (0.686 -> 0.677): exceptional durability.

pre_event.event_description: Three decades after independence, Mauritius -- a small, resource-poor, multi-ethnic Indian Ocean island (Hindu ~48%, Creole ~27%, Muslim ~17%, Sino-Mauritian ~3%) -- had built a prosperous, continuously democratic state (Freedom House 'Free') on textiles, tourism, financial services and institutional quality rather than natural resources.

Mauritius.notes: Inputs resolved live via mi.datasource (country_ref + year). WGI 2025-anchored 0-100. Genuinely multi-ethnic and genuinely democratic (the 'best loser' system manages communal representation); minimal natural resources -- prosperity is earned via institutions and human capital, not granted by rents. The institutional (not geographic, not authoritarian) version of small-island complexity control.

a_trajectory_ranking.prediction: Durable stable consolidation; Tier 2 maintained. High P1 + democratic accountability + low-complexity environment -> sustained stability and prosperity
a_trajectory_ranking.basis: P1 ordinality (high, 0.614); refined Strategy 3 -- institutional quality matching a low-complexity setting, achieved democratically
a_trajectory_ranking.falsification_condition: Loss of stability/prosperity, communal breakdown, or democratic reversion despite high P1

Mauritius.outcome_summary: Durable stable consolidation as predicted (Tier 2 held): MI 0.686 -> 0.677 (near-flat), P1 0.614 -> 0.637 (rose). Highest HDI in sub-Saharan Africa ('High Human Development'), among the continent's least corrupt and most democratic states, genuine multi-ethnic democracy with repeated peaceful turnovers including the November 2024 alternation. No communal breakdown.
key_events: highest HDI in sub-Saharan Africa sustained

analysis.overall_assessment: African democratic success cleanly confirmed, and the most durable record in the batch (near-flat MI, rising P1). The case shows the framework explains African success as well as African failure, and pins the mechanism on institutions + accountability rather than island geography.
analysis.what_this_case_uniquely_reveals: Refines Strategy 3 (complexity control) into an INSTITUTIONAL claim, not a geographic or authoritarian one: a genuinely multi-ethnic, genuinely democratic small island reaches Singapore-tier durability WITHOUT demographic engineering or constrained voice. Paired with Singapore (case7), Rwanda (case25) and Vietnam (case31), it completes the effectiveness/voice matrix -- Mauritius is the high-effectiveness/high-voice corner -- and is the rare entity whose institutions strengthened across the window.
analysis.baseline_impact: None; adds an independent African democratic-success data point and the high-voice corner of the effectiveness/voice comparison.
